title: The Cartographer blog
description: Short, cited articles from Team Cartographer on working with coding agents, with sources.

items.title: Praise is not evidence: appraising an agent's work honestly
items.summary: A confident all-done feels like proof, but it isn't. What research and vendor docs say about checking an agent's work against evidence, not tone.

items.title: Reading your own dead ends: what abandoned work can teach
items.summary: Abandoned branches and rewound sessions are the part of a build nobody keeps. Here's why they're worth reading, and what the docs say about keeping them.

items.title: Declaring done before you start: goals as a yardstick
items.summary: Decide what finished looks like before your first prompt. What Scrum and vendor docs say about done, and how to write a yardstick an agent can check.

items.title: Why a correction is the most informative prompt in a session
items.summary: A correction tells you what you meant, what the agent assumed, and where they split. Here's what research and vendor docs say, and how to read yours.

items.title: What the research says about reviewing code you didn't write
items.summary: Two studies of code review put understanding the change first. Here's what they found, and what it means when you didn't write the code.
